purpose: AC-EDIT-7: applyDeleteEditSignal (messageEdits/api.ts) rejects an edit/delete whose signal's authenticated sender (sender.pubkey, dispatcher-resolved) differs from the target message's stored authenticated sender (ChatMessage.senderPubkey, populated from the authenticated sender by S2's chatHandler.ts field-swap) — no tombstone written, no edit applied — unless the separate admin-delete path (GroupAdminsProvider, pre-existing from epic-group-invite-lifecycle's DD-11/AC-IMMUT-4/5) is satisfied. Verified this AC-EDIT-7 comparison was ALREADY correctly in place before this story (S2's mechanical field-swap plus the pre-existing S8/DD-11 admin carve-out already implement it byte-for-byte); this story is a hardening + test-completeness pass, not a logic rewrite. Also verifies (test-only, per scope) that chatPersistence.ts's TombstoneAuthorization re-check inherits the same authenticated value from this module for the third hop — confirmed: TombstoneAuthorization.senderPubkeyHex is populated exclusively from applyToKnownSlotCore's `incoming.senderPubkeyHex` (itself `sender?.pubkey ?? rumor.pubkey`), and chatPersistence.ts never reads rumor.pubkey or any forgeable field independently.

DELETE path: authorizeDeleteAgainstTarget(threadKey, knownRow.content, senderPubkey, knownRow.senderPubkey) — own-author for an ordinary message, current-admin-via-provider for a GROUP-thread informative-announcement message. Both paths derive senderPubkey as `sender?.pubkey ?? rumor.pubkey`, never independently reading rumor.pubkey as the compared value.
